items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: we made a record with Deborah Harry and the Jazz Passengers, you know Roy Nathanson... So Adam and I we did that together.

ctx.x: That’s a good one. What do your kids think of what you’ve done?

Well I have three sons. Two of them are in the music business. They think like anybody’s kids, you know, like he’s done some brilliant stuff and they also know I’m an idiot. So it’s an interesting relationship. Like I’ve made some records with my son Adam, who is an electronic artist under the name of Mocean Worker. And sometimes — we made a record with Deborah Harry and the Jazz Passengers, you know Roy Nathanson, a really cutting edge like Lower East Side group. And so Adam and I we did that together. So we did…

business. The first guy that gave him any shit would be laying on the floor and looking up, because he has less of anything than any of us. So he’s in the furniture business, he manages a chain of furniture stores in the northeast, and loves music. He’s a country music junkie and a fifties junkie. And it’s an odd question to ask, but he always says you do what you do.
